sources.title: Allan Adams, Nima Arkani-Hamed, Sergei Dubovsky, Alberto Nicolis, and Riccardo Rattazzi, Causality, Analyticity and an IR Obstruction to UV Completion
sources.locator: Complete relevant forward-dispersion passage in §4, PDF pp. 14–19, equations (19)–(24), (30), and analytic-structure discussion: crossing, pole residues, high-energy contour closure, optical-theorem sign, cut locations, and the role of an IR mass regulator.

contents.name: Equations (19)–(24): forward contour, crossing-even amplitude, pole residues, and optical-theorem spectral weight
contents.support: The source evaluates a forward contour with A(s)/s^3, pairs s/u poles under crossing, and replaces the discontinuity by the positive optical-theorem weight. The local theorem uses the same sign and contour logic in the shifted variable v, with all convergence and endpoint hypotheses stated explicitly.

contents.name: Equations (30)–(31) and Figure 8: IR-regulated massless-Goldstone cuts and subthreshold poles
contents.support: The source explains that a small mass moves the pair-production cuts away from the subtraction point and produces paired low-energy poles. The definition uses this only to motivate an explicit positive gap and pole-removal premise; it does not transfer the massless-limit conclusion.

contents.name: Strict positivity for an interacting example
contents.reason: The assigned conditional data do not require a nonzero absorptive part, so the theorem proves nonnegativity and permits equality rather than importing the source's stronger interacting-example conclusion.

sources.title: Claudia de Rham, Scott Melville, Andrew J. Tolley, and Shuang-Yong Zhou, Positivity Bounds for Scalar Theories
sources.locator: Complete five-page paper inspected; §§2.1–2.2, equations (1)–(15), PDF pp. 1–3: partial-wave unitarity, analyticity and two-subtraction growth, crossing and pole subtraction, and the positive forward dispersion moment.

contents.name: Equations (1)–(4): partial-wave normalization and forward optical-theorem sign
contents.support: The paper states the scalar partial-wave normalization and derives nonnegative forward absorptive data from partial-wave unitarity. The local definition records a compatible normalization only as context and adopts the forward sign as an explicit conditional input.

contents.name: Equations (5)–(11): analytic structure, two subtractions, pole removal, and crossing variable
contents.support: The paper deforms the contour around the two cuts and subthreshold poles, applies two subtractions, and uses s/u crossing to express the pole-subtracted amplitude through a positive spectral integral. The local proof gives a complete conditional argument for the forward slice.

contents.name: Equations (12)–(15): positive forward derivatives from positive integrals
contents.support: The forward specialization makes each even derivative a positive dispersive moment. The finite Hankel and interval-localizer inequalities are derived locally by representing the normalized coefficients as moments on 0 < x ≤ 1; these particular matrix tests are not attributed to the paper.

contents.name: Away-forward bounds and UV-completion conclusions
contents.reason: The batch is restricted to the forward gapped identical-scalar data and finite necessary tests; nonforward bounds and model-specific UV-completion claims require additional hypotheses and are not included.

contents.name: Equations (13)–(15) specialized to the order-two finite test
contents.support: The source supplies the positive forward moments underlying the necessary coefficient constraints. The strict passing and excluded regions, determinant 1/12, and negative witness -1/8 are derived directly in the example; no numeric vector or region classification is attributed to the paper.

sources.title: Ivano Basile, Luca Buoninfante, Francesco Di Filippo, Benjamin Knorr, Alessia Platania, and Anna Tokareva, Lectures in Quantum Gravity
sources.locator: Complete 303-page lecture-notes PDF retrieved; §§3.2.1–3.2.3 and 3.3.1, printed pp. 90–98 (PDF pp. 94–97): analyticity, partial waves, Martin–Froissart growth, and the simplest forward positivity bound.

contents.name: Section 3.2.1: analyticity properties of scattering amplitudes
contents.support: The notes describe fixed-transfer analyticity away from real cuts and connect it to dispersion arguments. The item explicitly specifies a two-cut domain and declares analyticity as input rather than claiming to derive it from causality.

contents.name: Section 3.2.2: partial-wave expansion and unitarity
contents.support: The notes derive partial-wave unitarity and its relation to the optical theorem. The local definition states a compatible convention and uses only the resulting forward absorptive sign as an assumption.

contents.name: Section 3.2.3: Martin–Froissart bound
contents.support: The notes explain why a mass gap controls high-energy growth and permits a twice-subtracted relation. The local input instead states the precise uniform o(|v|^2) upper-half-plane condition needed by its shifted-contour proof.

contents.name: Section 3.3.1: the simplest positivity bound
contents.support: The notes derive the forward coefficient sign from analyticity, unitarity, crossing, and the twice-subtracted dispersion relation. The authored result keeps every hypothesis conditional and proves the moment identity locally.

contents.name: The notes' status as a SciPost Physics Lecture Notes submission
contents.support: The PDF front matter identifies this as a lecture-notes submission and leaves publication fields blank. The source table records it as complete lecture notes, not a final published book.

sources.locator: Actually read in this repair: Section 2 PDF pp. 7–9 and Appendix B PDF pp. 33–34; full 42-page PDF retrieved, other sections not claimed read.

contents.name: Single versus multiple EOM insertions; Jacobian and source transformation boundary
contents.support: Appendix B explicitly distinguishes the vanishing one-insertion residue from nonvanishing two-insertion result.
